```{r m6-setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", out.width = "100%")
options(width = 82)
```

Three different kinds of uncertainty can arise in a posterior grading analysis:

1. **Posterior uncertainty** about the entity targets \(\theta\) under your
   statistical model (for example, a `0.45` probability that `A` is below `B`).
2. **Monte Carlo approximation error** from estimating pairwise probabilities
   and expected losses with a finite sample of simulation draws \(S\).
3. **Model misspecification**—differences between your statistical model (or
   fixed empirical-Bayes prior) and the actual population.

Drawing more posterior samples shrinks Monte Carlo error without shrinking
posterior uncertainty or fixing a misspecified model. This article explains
`postrank`'s Monte Carlo diagnostics (`postrank_diagnose()`), an MCSE screen
for borderline pairs (`postrank_mc_fragility()`), split-sample cross-fitting
(`postrank_crossfit()`), and conditional fixed-sample IID bounds
(`postrank_iid_bounds()`, `postrank_regret_bound()`,
`postrank_protection_envelopes()`, `postrank_protection_analysis()`). Every
executed chunk uses small synthetic draw datasets and stored results without
model fitting or optimization.

**Diagnostics are descriptive summaries, not guarantees.** Monte Carlo standard
errors, MCMC effective sample sizes, `R-hat` checks, fragility counts, and
cross-fitting differences are descriptive summaries of simulation variation on
your supplied draws; they do not guarantee convergence, finite-sample coverage,
or model adequacy.

## Pairwise Monte Carlo standard errors {#start-with-one-direction-on-one-criterion}

On criterion `k`, the directional-error probability
\(e_{ij,k} = \Pr(\theta_{ik} \le \theta_{jk})\) is estimated from \(S\)
equal-weight draws by the sample average of the `0/1` indicator
\(\mathbf{1}\{\theta_{ik}^{(s)} \le \theta_{jk}^{(s)}\}\). A value near `0.5`
means the model itself is uncertain about which entity ranks higher; the Monte
Carlo standard error (MCSE) measures how much that sample average varies across
simulation runs of size \(S\).

`postrank_toy` holds `32` independent (`regime = "iid"`) joint draws for three
fictional sites on two criteria (`32` draws is tiny—used here so numerical
errors are large enough to inspect). Passing a one-row `pairs` data frame to
`postrank_diagnose()` computes the indicator trace and MCSE for `001` ahead of
`site-B` on `need_A`:

```{r m6-iid-pair}
library(postrank)

pair <- data.frame(
  entity_i = "001", entity_j = "site-B", criterion_id = "need_A"
)
iid_diagnostic <- postrank_diagnose(postrank_toy, pairs = pair)
pair_summary <- iid_diagnostic[["summaries"]][["pair_1"]]
z_iid <- iid_diagnostic[["traces"]][["pair_1"]][["values"]]
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Draws = length(z_iid),
  Estimated_probability = mean(z_iid),
  MCSE = pair_summary[["diagnostics"]][["mcse_mean"]][["value"]],
  SD_over_sqrt_S = sd(z_iid) / sqrt(length(z_iid))
), digits = 4)
```

For independent draws, the MCSE equals the sample standard deviation divided by
\(\sqrt{S}\)—for a `0/1` indicator with sample mean \(\widehat{p}\),
\(\sqrt{\widehat{p}(1 - \widehat{p}) / (S - 1)}\) (`0.0778` here at
\(\widehat{p} = 0.25\), \(S = 32\)). Pointwise MCSEs describe one pair at a
time; they do not form simultaneous bands across all pairs or give the
posterior probability that a full grading is right. See Lee (2026), Chapter 21,
[Monte Carlo error under a declared sampling law](https://joonho112.github.io/postrank-theory-book/chapters/21-numerical-uncertainty.html#sec-monte-carlo-coefficients).

## Loss traces for a fixed grading {#diagnose-the-loss-of-a-declared-report}

When you also pass a fixed integer `grade` vector and `settings` to
`postrank_diagnose()`, it evaluates criterion-specific and weighted total losses
draw by draw. On joint `S x n x K` draws, criteria are combined **within each
joint draw `s`**, preserving cross-criterion simulation covariance rather than
treating separate criterion MCSEs as independent. On `postrank_toy`,
`postrank_diagnose()` returns the IID standard error of the fixed `1/2/2`
grading's weighted loss while recording `convergence_verified = FALSE` and
`finite_sample_certificate = FALSE`:

```{r diagnostics}
toy_grade <- setNames(c(1L, 2L, 2L), postrank_toy[["entity_ids"]])
diagnostics <- postrank_diagnose(postrank_toy, grade = toy_grade,
  settings = list(weights = c(need_A = 0.6, need_B = 0.4),
    tau = 0.25, G_max = 3L))
diagnostics[["summaries"]][["weighted_total_loss"]][["diagnostics"]][["mcse_mean"]]
c(convergence_verified = diagnostics[["convergence_verified"]],
  finite_sample_certificate = diagnostics[["finite_sample_certificate"]])
```

`pr_toy_mcmc` stores four independent two-state Markov chains of `512`
iterations each (`S = 2,048` total, no warmup or thinning) with transition
probabilities `0.012` (`0 -> 1`) and `0.048` (`1 -> 0`). Its true stationary
probability of state `1` is `0.2000`, with strong serial autocorrelation:

```{r m6-mcmc-run}
law <- attr(pr_toy_mcmc, "law")
mcmc <- postrank_draws(
  pr_toy_mcmc, regime = "mcmc", chains = 4L,
  warmup_per_chain = 0L, thin = 1L, declarations = law[["declarations"]]
)
diagnostic <- postrank_diagnose(
  mcmc,
  grade = c(A = 1L, B = 2L, C = 3L),
  settings = list(weights = c(k1 = 0.6, k2 = 0.4), tau = 0.25),
  pairs = data.frame(entity_i = "A", entity_j = "B", criterion_id = "k1")
)
```

```{r m6-mcmc-table}
selected <- diagnostic[["summaries"]][c("pair_1", "weighted_total_loss")]
diagnostic_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(selected, function(s) {
  d <- s[["diagnostics"]]
  data.frame(
    Mean = s[["mean"]], MCSE = d[["mcse_mean"]][["value"]],
    ESS_mean = d[["ess_mean"]][["value"]], Rhat = d[["rhat"]][["value"]],
    ESS_tail = d[["ess_tail"]][["value"]]
  )
}))
rownames(diagnostic_table) <- c("A ahead of B: k1 error", "Fixed 1/2/3: weighted loss")
knitr::kable(diagnostic_table, digits = 4)
```

On this two-state construction, the `A ahead of B` indicator equals the state-`1`
indicator (pooled sample mean `353 / 2048 = 0.1724` vs. true `0.2000`), and the
fixed `1/2/3` grading's draw-wise loss equals `2/15 + (2/3) * indicator`
(estimated loss `0.2482` vs. true `4/15 = 0.2667`; MCSE `0.0384 = (2/3) * 0.0576`).
Per-criterion traces are stored separately in `criterion_risk_1` and
`criterion_risk_2` (with separate criterion draw matrices, per-criterion traces
are available while `weighted_total_loss` MCSE is unavailable; under
`objective = "minimax"`, the weighted trace is auxiliary rather than an MCSE for
\(\max_k R_k(g)\)).

## Reading MCMC diagnostics {#what-the-mcmc-metrics-actually-summarize}

For equal-length, regularly thinned chains, `postrank_diagnose()` delegates
scalar chain summaries to the `posterior` package (`rhat`, `ess_bulk`,
`ess_tail`, `ess_mean`, and `mcse_mean` on split chains). These are univariate
summaries per trace, distinct from multivariate effective sample size; see Lee
(2026), Chapter 21,
[Multivariate output analysis and effective sample size](https://joonho112.github.io/postrank-theory-book/chapters/21-numerical-uncertainty.html#sec-mcmc-output-analysis).

On `0/1` indicator traces, quantile indicators at `0.05` or `0.95` can be
constant, producing `ESS_tail = NA` (recorded with `available = FALSE` and an
explicit `unavailable_reason`, never silently replaced by `0`). Conversely, an
all-zero empirical indicator trace can simply mean a rare ordering reversal was
never visited during the run. Unequal chain lengths keep all draws in pooled
means without truncating or padding chains to compute cross-chain `R-hat` or
ESS, and single-chain runs cannot check between-chain agreement.

In `pr_toy_mcmc`, `Rhat` is `1.0905` (above the `1.01` heuristic) and both
`ESS_mean` and `ess_bulk` are `42.95` (below `400`, i.e., `100` per chain
across `4` chains), triggering three exploration warnings in
`diagnostic$warnings`. Comparing the MCMC MCSE to a naive IID `sd / sqrt(S)`
calculation shows why ignoring autocorrelation is misleading:

```{r m6-chain-comparison}
pair_trace <- diagnostic[["traces"]][["pair_1"]][["values"]]
chain_means <- diagnostic[["summaries"]][["pair_1"]][["chain_means"]]
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Chain = names(chain_means), Estimated_probability = unname(chain_means)
), digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)
c(
  MCMC_MCSE = diagnostic_table[["MCSE"]][1],
  Naive_IID_SD_over_sqrt_S = sd(pair_trace) / sqrt(length(pair_trace))
)
```

Treating the `2,048` autocorrelated draws as independent would understate the
MCSE by nearly sevenfold (`0.0083` vs. `0.0576`). Likewise, **effective sample
size (ESS) cannot be plugged into an IID concentration inequality in place of
\(S\)** (`postrank` does not issue finite-sample concentration certificates for
MCMC chains).

## Fixed gradings versus data-selected gradings {#a-fixed-action-and-a-selected-action-need-different-interpretations}

Evaluating `postrank_diagnose()` on a `grade` vector chosen *before* looking at
the draws estimates the loss of that fixed grading. When you pass a solved `fit`
instead, `postrank_diagnose()` checks that `fit` came from the same input and
labels the trace summaries as post-selection descriptive summaries: optimizing
grades on the same draws introduces selection optimism that pointwise MCSEs do
not capture.

Note two special cases:

- If a grading places every entity in Grade 1 (`N = 0`), its weighted loss is
  identically \(\tau\) on every draw (`structural_constant_from_action`, zero
  loss variance, `E_over_N = NA`), even if individual entity targets mix poorly.
- Externally supplied `postrank_probabilities()` carry no draw history, so MCSE
  and ESS cannot be recovered from them; `postrank_coefficient_diagnose()` on
  `hyperparameter_mcmc` mixtures diagnoses integration over conditional normal
  expectations rather than entity-draw dispersion (see
  [Posterior representations and pairwise comparison probabilities](m3-posterior-inputs.html)).

## Fragility and split-sample cross-fitting {#sensitivity-and-cross-fitting-answer-narrower-questions}

Two fast summaries in `postrank()` probe sensitivity to simulation noise on
joint target draws:

- **Borderline-pair fragility (`postrank_mc_fragility()`, requested by default via `fragility = TRUE`).**
  For each unordered pair, `postrank` compares the weighted error probability in
  its likelier direction (\(\min\{\bar{e}_{ij}, \bar{e}_{ji}\}\)) against
  \(\tau\), flagging pairs whose distance from \(\tau\) is strictly less than
  `z` (default `2`) times that pair's directional MCSE. Because grades are
  chosen jointly under transitivity and `G_max`, a borderline pair need not flip
  any grade (and a non-borderline pair can still move when neighbors shift). On
  MCMC inputs, only pairs strictly within `screen_margin = 0.1` of \(\tau\) are
  traced for speed, recording an informational `"MCMC screen"` note in
  `warnings`.
- **Two-fold draw cross-fitting (`postrank_crossfit()`, requested via `crossfit = TRUE`).**
  Splits retained draws into two folds (halves for IID; groups of whole chains
  for multi-chain MCMC, or halves for a single chain), optimizes a grading on
  each fold (requiring a solver such as `highs` or licensed Gurobi), and
  evaluates that grading on the held-out fold. Under independent IID folds and
  pre-fixed weighted settings, the held-out evaluation is an unbiased estimate
  of the **fold grading's** posterior expected loss (and `mean_abs_optimism`
  avoids sign cancellation when both folds pick the same grades). Cross-fitting
  splits posterior draws from your existing model fit—it does not refit the
  statistical model on held-out observations, does not make dependent MCMC
  chains independent, does not apply unbiasedness to the nonlinear `minimax`
  maximum, and does not bias-correct the full-sample loss.
- **Prefix and subset stability (`stability` in `postrank_diagnose()`).**
  Optionally re-solves the problem (requiring a solver, up to `12` single-thread
  solves) across MCMC draw `prefixes` or `chain_subsets` or across perturbed
  `settings_grid` entries (on IID inputs, only full-draw `settings_grid`
  overrides are supported), keeping all successful and failed solve records for
  descriptive comparison.

On `postrank_toy`, we can inspect the stored two-fold cross-fit (`toy_crossfit`)
alongside `postrank_mc_fragility()` on the stored weighted fit (`toy_analysis`):

```{r mc-diagnostics}
cf <- postrank_example("toy_crossfit")
cf
toy_fit <- postrank_example("toy_analysis")[["fit"]]
postrank_mc_fragility(postrank_toy, fit = toy_fit)[["summary"]]
```

## Conditional fixed-sample IID bounds {#conditional-iid-bounds-cover-a-different-calculation}

Unlike pointwise MCSEs, `postrank_iid_bounds()` computes an analytic
simultaneous error radius across all \(M = \binom{n}{2}\) unordered pairs on
each criterion when draws are independent (`regime = "iid"`) and the sample size
was fixed in advance. Because standard `postrank` inputs are tie-free
(\(e_{ji,k} = 1 - e_{ij,k}\)), bounding one direction per unordered pair bounds
both directions, giving `2M` events per criterion (rather than `4M` in a
tie-permitting formulation; tie-aware mode does not provide these IID helpers).
With positive criterion error budgets \(\alpha_k\) summing to at most \(\alpha\),
the radius on criterion \(k\) is

\[
\varepsilon_k = \min\!\left\{1,
  \sqrt{\frac{\log(2M / \alpha_k)}{2 S_k}}\right\}.
\]

**IID bounds and protection envelopes hold only under their stated conditions:**

- Every criterion uses equal-weight independent (`regime = "iid"`) entity-joint
  draws (pairs and criteria need not be independent of one another; MCMC draws
  are rejected because ESS is not an IID sample size).
- Draw counts \(S_k\) and allocations \(\alpha_k\) were fixed before sampling,
  with `adaptive_stopping = FALSE` (`design` records your declaration without
  verifying it externally).
- The \(1 - \alpha\) coverage statement refers to repeated Monte Carlo sampling
  from the same fixed posterior—it is not a posterior probability that a grading
  is right and does not check model specification.
- Formulas are evaluated in ordinary floating-point arithmetic without interval
  enclosures, so `guarantee_issued` and `numerically_verified` remain `FALSE`
  (`guarantee_status = "conditional_bound"`).

For `postrank_toy`, the synthetic generator fixed \(S = 32\) and
\(\alpha_1 = \alpha_2 = 0.025\) (\(\alpha = 0.05\)) before sampling:

```{r iid-reference}
bounds <- postrank_iid_bounds(
  postrank_toy, alpha = 0.05,
  alpha_by_criterion = c(need_A = 0.025, need_B = 0.025),
  design = list(
    sample_sizes_fixed_before_sampling = TRUE,
    alpha_fixed_before_sampling = TRUE,
    adaptive_stopping = FALSE,
    planned_sample_sizes = c(need_A = 32L, need_B = 32L),
    declaration_note = "Prespecified in the bundled synthetic Normal generator"
  )
)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Criterion = names(bounds[["epsilon"]]),
  Radius = unname(bounds[["epsilon"]])
), digits = 4)
bounds[c("guarantee_status", "bound_computed", "numerically_verified",
  "finite_sample_certificate", "guarantee_issued")]
```

Write \(\delta_w = \sum_{k=1}^K w_k \varepsilon_k\). On the simultaneous
\(1 - \alpha\) event where every \(|\widehat{e}_{ij,k} - e_{ij,k}| \le \varepsilon_k\),
the empirical weighted loss of any fixed grading with \(N\) ordered pairs
differs from its true posterior weighted loss by at most \((N / M) \delta_w\).
Moreover, over any non-empty grading family fixed before sampling (`G_max` or
`exact_G`, with `objective = "weighted"` and `q = NULL`), a checked grading
\(\widehat{g}\) with verified whole-problem solver gap \(\eta = U - L\) has true
posterior weighted-loss regret at most \(2 \delta_w + \eta\).
`postrank_regret_bound()` evaluates that bound on a matching `postrank_fit`
(bounding loss regret, not equality of grade vectors, and rejecting raw,
relative, or candidate-only gaps):

```{r m6-regret-bound}
toy <- postrank_example("toy_analysis")
regret <- postrank_regret_bound(toy[["fit"]], bounds)
regret[c("delta_w", "eta", "regret_upper_bound", "guarantee_status")]
```

When a weighted problem carries empirical error budgets `q`
(\(\widehat{E}_k(g) \le q_k N(g)\)), Monte Carlo error also affects which
gradings appear feasible. `postrank_protection_envelopes()` constructs two
shifted problems without running a solver:

- `inner_problem`: tightened constraints \(\widehat{E}_k(g) \le (q_k - \varepsilon_k) N(g)\);
- `outer_problem`: relaxed constraints \(\widehat{E}_k(g) \le (q_k + \varepsilon_k) N(g)\).

The signed coefficients \(q_k \mp \varepsilon_k\) are not clipped to `(0, 1)`,
and zero-weight protected criteria still use their own \(\varepsilon_k\). When
\(q_k - \varepsilon_k < 0\), no grading with \(N > 0\) can satisfy the inner
row, so an infeasible `inner_problem` does not prove that the true
\(q\)-constrained problem is infeasible. Passing the envelope to
`postrank_protection_analysis()` solves both problems sequentially (requiring an
optimization solver such as `highs` or licensed Gurobi) and combines the checked
`inner` upper bound (`inner_risk_upper`) with the **whole-problem `outer` lower
bound** (`outer_whole_problem_risk_lower`—never substituting the inner lower
bound) to report `computed_value` equal to
`inner_risk_upper - outer_whole_problem_risk_lower + 2 * delta_w`
(`status = "diagnostic_only"`, `guarantee_issued = FALSE`). See Lee (2026),
Chapter 21,
[Effects of coefficient error on risk and feasibility](https://joonho112.github.io/postrank-theory-book/chapters/21-numerical-uncertainty.html#sec-coefficient-error),
and Appendix D,
[Numerical helpers and their conditions](https://joonho112.github.io/postrank-theory-book/appendices/D-package-correspondence.html#conditional-numerical-helpers).

## Separating numerical precision from model adequacy {#numerical-accuracy-leaves-model-adequacy-to-be-assessed}

Solver gaps bound optimization error on the numbers passed to the solver, and
MCSEs or IID radii describe how closely finite simulation draws approximate your
supplied posterior. Neither quantity measures whether your statistical model
matches reality: a tiny solver gap and a tiny MCSE can still accompany a
misspecified likelihood or prior. See Lee (2026), Chapter 24,
[Self-reported error and calibration](https://joonho112.github.io/postrank-theory-book/chapters/24-misspecification-calibration.html#sec-self-reported-calibration).

In plug-in empirical Bayes, posterior probabilities condition on an estimated
prior distribution \(\widehat{G}\) (not to be confused with the grade count
\(G\)); drawing more posterior samples while holding \(\widehat{G}\) fixed does
not propagate uncertainty in estimating \(\widehat{G}\). Hierarchical models
integrate over the hyperparameter uncertainty specified by their prior, yet
external calibration and measurement validity still require substantive
model checking outside `postrank`; see Lee (2026), Chapter 24,
[Hyperparameters, precision and represented uncertainty](https://joonho112.github.io/postrank-theory-book/chapters/24-misspecification-calibration.html#sec-producer-model-error).

See also
[Computing grades, choosing settings, and reading solver bounds](m5-computing-grades.html)
for solver statuses and lower bounds, and
[Exact ties in the posterior versus withheld comparisons](m4-ties-and-withholding.html)
for tie-aware mode.
